content.chapter: Chapter 3: A Baby in the River
objectives: I can follow the basket from the river to the palace.
I can explain how the mother’s trust in Allah was stronger than her sadness.
I can use but for contrast and a who-clause to add information about a person.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Explain why the chapter says “The basket was carried away by the waters” (the passive keeps the basket in focus), complete the lines with but, also, while and Soon, then rebuild the sentence about the queen with the extra information “who was different from her husband” between commas.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: SHEL-ter, a-SHORE, SER-vants, kind-HEART-ed. Say the name as A-si-ye. Read the who-clause with a small pause at each comma.
content.lessonPlan: Look at The Basket hotspot. How could a basket keep a baby safe on a river? Listen once and follow the journey of the basket. Read the middle of the chapter again and mark the sentence that joins sadness and trust with but.
discussionPoints: The mother was sad, but she trusted Allah and did what she was told. What is the difference between feeling trust and acting with trust?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “The Basket” and “Queen Asiye”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the middle of the chapter. Read the part after but in the sentence about her sadness. Check who followed the basket and when Queen Asiye saw the baby, then try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a person who receives guidance, feels worried and then makes a decision. Use an instruction, a passive sentence, but, while or when, and will for the decision.

whatToNotice: The chapter follows the basket: the mother, the river, the waves, the shore, the palace servants and the queen.
Notice “The basket was carried away by the waters.” The passive keeps the focus on the basket, not on the mother.
readListen: Look at The Basket hotspot. How could a basket keep a baby safe on a river?
Listen once and follow the journey of the basket.
Read the middle of the chapter again and mark the sentence that joins sadness and trust with but.
Open the picture hotspots “The Basket” and “Queen Asiye” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find Allah’s three instructions to the mother and what she did.
Middle: Find who followed the basket and what the mother knew about Allah.
End: Find where the waves took the basket, what Queen Asiye felt and what she decided.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: shelter, ashore, servants, kind-hearted.
“Waters will carry it to the shelter.” What was the real shelter for baby Moses in the end?
Write one sentence with kind-hearted about a person you know.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The question asks what gave the mother comfort. The answer is in the middle of the chapter, in the sentence that starts “She was so sad, but”.
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the middle of the chapter.
Read the part after but in the sentence about her sadness.
Check who followed the basket and when Queen Asiye saw the baby, then try again.
selfCheck: Can I retell the journey of the basket in four steps?
Can I explain the contrast between sadness and trust?
Can I add information about a person with who between commas?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a person who receives guidance, feels worried and then makes a decision. Use an instruction, a passive sentence, but, while or when, and will for the decision.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Tell the chapter in five steps. Use first, then, next, soon and finally.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “The basket was carried away by the waters.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, how baby Moses reached the palace.

thinkAloud.sentence: Soon, the waves brought the basket ashore near the Pharaoh’s palace.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: I see a small basket on the big river. The waves carry it gently. It stops on the shore near a great palace, and servants come to look at it. Close your eyes and add one more detail from the text.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “than she could be.”
stopAndCheck.question: What did Moses’s mother tell her daughter to do? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: The mother was sad, but she trusted Allah and did what she was told. What is the difference between feeling trust and acting with trust?

objectives: I can explain how three people helped bring Moses (pbuh) back to his mother.
I can describe how Moses grew up and where he felt he belonged.
I can choose between to (purpose), because of and because (reason).
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Match words such as immediately, nearby and felt close to with their meanings, complete three lines with to, because of and because, then fix three mistakes: will be, became and willing to help.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: COUR-age, o-RIG-i-nal-ly, im-ME-di-ate-ly. Nurse has one syllable. Read the sister’s words quickly and with excitement: “I know a good woman. She lives nearby.”
content.lessonPlan: Look at The Nurse hotspot. Why does a palace need a nurse for a baby? Listen once and follow who speaks and who acts. Read the end of the chapter again and underline the reason Moses felt close to the Children of Israel.
discussionPoints: People always remember Queen Asiye for her goodness and courage. Who do you remember for their goodness, and what did they do?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “The Nurse” and “A Loving Home”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Find each person in the first half of the chapter: Queen Asiye, Moses’s sister and his mother. Read who speaks first, who answers her and who comes to the palace. Match again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a person who receives help, grows over time and develops a sense of responsibility or belonging. Use an instruction, to for purpose, because or because of, became for change and always for a lasting quality.

whatToNotice: Each woman has a part: The queen asks for a nurse, the sister suggests a woman, and the mother comes to the palace. The chapter says “Allah is the Best Protector.”
Notice the time jump “Years passed and Moses became a strong young man.” Became shows a change into a new stage of life.
readListen: Look at The Nurse hotspot. Why does a palace need a nurse for a baby?
Listen once and follow who speaks and who acts.
Read the end of the chapter again and underline the reason Moses felt close to the Children of Israel.
Open the picture hotspots “The Nurse” and “A Loving Home” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find the queen’s order to her servants and what Moses’s sister said to the Queen.
Middle: Find who looked after Moses and why people always remember Queen Asiye.
End: Find what Moses knew about the Pharaoh and why he felt close to the Children of Israel.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: nurse, courage, raised, originally.
“he was originally not from a family of the palace”: What does originally tell you about Moses?
Write one sentence with courage and one with raised.
content.quickChallengeGuide: You will match three people with what each one did. Read the first half of the chapter and note one action for the queen, the sister and the mother.
wrongAnswerSupport: Find each person in the first half of the chapter: Queen Asiye, Moses’s sister and his mother.
Read who speaks first, who answers her and who comes to the palace.
Match again.
selfCheck: Can I explain how Moses came back to his mother?
Can I give one purpose with to and one reason with because?
Can I describe Moses as a young man with became and always?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a person who receives help, grows over time and develops a sense of responsibility or belonging. Use an instruction, to for purpose, because or because of, became for change and always for a lasting quality.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Explain in two sentences why young Moses felt close to the Israelites.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “People always remember her because of her goodness and courage.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, how Moses’s sister brought her mother to the palace.

thinkAloud.sentence: She said to her servants, “Find a nurse for the baby.”
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: The queen needs a nurse, and Moses’s sister saw everything. I think the sister will bring their mother to the palace. Make your own guess, then read on and check it.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “raised him in the palace with love.”
stopAndCheck.question: How did Moses go back to his mother? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: People always remember Queen Asiye for her goodness and courage. Who do you remember for their goodness, and what did they do?

content.chapter: Chapter 5: A Mistake in the Bazaar
objectives: I can separate what Moses (pbuh) did by accident from what he did next.
I can explain how Moses understood that the man was quarrelsome.
I can use while + past continuous for a background action.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Decide what “while Moses (pbuh) was walking in the bazaar” tells you about the order of actions, choose saw, who and that, then match short spoken lines such as “Forgive me!” and “I have wronged myself” with what the speaker is doing: asking, admitting or accusing.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: ac-ci-DEN-tal-ly, QUAR-rel-some, PEACE-a-ble, PAR-doned. Say “Forgive me!” as a sincere request, and “Are you going to kill me too?” as an accusation, not a real question.
content.lessonPlan: Look at the Forgiveness hotspot. What did Moses ask Allah for? Listen once and follow the two days. Read the chapter again and circle One day, Suddenly and The next day.
discussionPoints: Moses said, “I have wronged myself.” Why is it important to admit a mistake, even when it was not on purpose?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “The Mistake” and “Forgiveness”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the beginning of the chapter. Read the two sentences just before “Moses was very upset.” Check when the man made fun of Moses, then try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different tense situation in a public place. Use while + past continuous, suddenly, a who-clause, understood that … and a question with going to.

whatToNotice: The chapter has two days: On the first day Moses causes a death by accident and asks for forgiveness; on the next day the same man is fighting again.
Notice “I didn’t do it on purpose. I have wronged myself.” Moses admits his mistake and does not hide it.
readListen: Look at the Forgiveness hotspot. What did Moses ask Allah for?
Listen once and follow the two days.
Read the chapter again and circle One day, Suddenly and The next day.
Open the picture hotspots “The Mistake” and “Forgiveness” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find what Moses saw while he was walking and what the weak man called out.
Middle: Find what Moses said in his prayer and why Allah pardoned him.
End: Find what Moses understood about the man and how the man made fun of him.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: accidentally, pardoned, quarrelsome, peaceable.
“a quarrelsome man, not a peaceable man”: How are the two words opposites?
Write one sentence with accidentally and one with pardoned.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The question asks why Moses prayed “Forgive me!”. Look at what happened just before the prayer, at the beginning of the chapter.
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the beginning of the chapter.
Read the two sentences just before “Moses was very upset.”
Check when the man made fun of Moses, then try again.
selfCheck: Can I explain the difference between an accident and an action on purpose?
Can I describe how Moses took responsibility?
Can I use while + was/were + -ing with a past simple event?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different tense situation in a public place. Use while + past continuous, suddenly, a who-clause, understood that … and a question with going to.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Compare the two days in two sentences. Use “The next day”.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “Moses was very upset.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, what happened in the bazaar on the second day.

thinkAloud.sentence: The man once more called out to Moses, “Help me!”
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: Who is “The man”? The sentence before says it was the same man from the Children of Israel whom Moses helped the day before. Find one more he, she or they and say who it is.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “This is of Satan’s doing.”
stopAndCheck.question: What did Moses say to Allah after his mistake? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: Moses said, “I have wronged myself.” Why is it important to admit a mistake, even when it was not on purpose?

objectives: I can explain why Moses (pbuh) had to leave Egypt.
I can explain why Midian was a safer place for him.
I can use be going to for a prediction based on what is happening now.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Explain why the man says “Now they are going to catch you” (a prediction from what is already happening), put five parts of the journey in order from Egypt to Midian, then fix three mistakes: where for a place, who for people and the question order Why are you sitting.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: PUN-ish-ment, es-CAPED, CAT-tle, MID-i-an. The -ed in escaped sounds like /t/. Read the warning with urgency: “Run away from the city.”
content.lessonPlan: Look at A Warning hotspot. Who warned Moses, and where did he come from? Listen once and follow Moses from Egypt to Midian. Read the middle of the chapter again and find the sentence about who ruled Midian.
discussionPoints: A man came from the far end of the city to warn Moses. Why is it important to warn someone who is in danger, even a person you do not know well?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “A Warning” and “The Well in Midian”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the middle of the chapter. Read the sentence after “he reached the land of Midian”. Decide if the statement matches it, then try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about someone who must leave a place quickly and arrives somewhere new. Use the present continuous for a danger now, be going to, an urgent instruction, after + time and a Why are you …? question.

whatToNotice: The chapter moves from danger (a warning) to a long journey and then to a new scene at a well.
Notice “The Pharaoh’s soldiers are looking for you.” The present continuous shows the search is already happening, so the man predicts “Now they are going to catch you.”
readListen: Look at A Warning hotspot. Who warned Moses, and where did he come from?
Listen once and follow Moses from Egypt to Midian.
Read the middle of the chapter again and find the sentence about who ruled Midian.
Open the picture hotspots “A Warning” and “The Well in Midian” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find the man’s warning and his advice to Moses.
Middle: Find what Moses knew about the punishment and where he arrived after many days.
End: Find who was at the well and what Moses asked the two girls.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: punishment, escaped, cattle, well.
“He was not alone as Allah guided him.” What does as mean in this sentence?
Write one sentence with escaped and one with punishment.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The statement is about who ruled the land of Midian. Find the short sentence about the ruler in the middle of the chapter, just after Moses reaches Midian.
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the middle of the chapter.
Read the sentence after “he reached the land of Midian”.
Decide if the statement matches it, then try again.
selfCheck: Can I explain why Moses left Egypt?
Can I say why Midian was safer?
Can I make a prediction with be going to from something I can see now?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about someone who must leave a place quickly and arrives somewhere new. Use the present continuous for a danger now, be going to, an urgent instruction, after + time and a Why are you …? question.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Explain in three sentences how Moses reached Midian.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “He was not alone as Allah guided him.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, why Moses left Egypt and where he went.

thinkAloud.sentence: Moses escaped from the soldiers.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: I want to sum up this chapter. A man warned Moses, he left Egypt, and after many days he came to a well in Midian. My sentence is: Moses ran away from Egypt and found a new land where the Pharaoh did not rule. Sum up the next paragraph in one sentence.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “Run away from the city.”
stopAndCheck.question: What did the man from the far end of the city tell Moses? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: A man came from the far end of the city to warn Moses. Why is it important to warn someone who is in danger, even a person you do not know well?

objectives: I can explain why the two sisters had to wait at the well.
I can describe how the help of Moses (pbuh) changed their day.
I can use have to and did not have to for necessity and no necessity.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Decide what “We did not have to wait” means (it was not necessary), complete the sisters’ explanation with cannot, So and until, then turn a That’s why-result into a because-reason and say There are no young men with do not have any.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: SHEP-herds, MES-sen-ger, PA-tient. The h in shepherds is silent: SHEP-erds. In have to, the v sounds like f: HAF-ta.
content.lessonPlan: Look at the Waiting Their Turn hotspot. Why did the girls not go near the water? Listen once and follow the sisters’ explanation. Read the middle of the chapter again and find what the sisters told their father.
discussionPoints: Moses first understood what the sisters needed, and then he helped. Why is it important to listen before you help someone?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “Waiting Their Turn” and “Helping Others”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the middle of the chapter. Read the sisters’ answer to their father, especially the sentence with did not have to. Check who helped the sheep drink, then try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about people who usually have to do something difficult but get unexpected help one day. Use cannot, have to, until, a past action that changes the situation and did not have to.

whatToNotice: The sisters give a chain of reasons: their father is very old and there are no young men at home, so they have to do the work themselves.
Notice “We did not have to wait until the other shepherds went away.” Did not have to means it was not necessary; it does not mean it was not allowed.
readListen: Look at the Waiting Their Turn hotspot. Why did the girls not go near the water?
Listen once and follow the sisters’ explanation.
Read the middle of the chapter again and find what the sisters told their father.
Open the picture hotspots “Waiting Their Turn” and “Helping Others” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find three reasons the sisters had to water the sheep themselves.
Middle: Find what Moses understood and what he did.
End: Find who the sisters’ father was and why he sent the girls alone.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: turn, shepherds, messenger, very old.
“We have to wait our turn.” What does turn mean here?
Write one sentence about a time you had to wait your turn.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The question asks why the sisters got home early. Find what the sisters told their father when he asked “What happened?”, in the middle of the chapter.
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the middle of the chapter.
Read the sisters’ answer to their father, especially the sentence with did not have to.
Check who helped the sheep drink, then try again.
selfCheck: Can I give two reasons the sisters had to wait?
Can I explain what Moses noticed before he helped?
Can I explain the difference between have to and did not have to?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about people who usually have to do something difficult but get unexpected help one day. Use cannot, have to, until, a past action that changes the situation and did not have to.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Write a short dialogue between the sisters and their father.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “Moses (pbuh) understood that the two sisters needed help.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, how Moses helped the two sisters.

thinkAloud.sentence: That’s why he had to send the girls alone.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: “That’s why” points back to the sentence before: Prophet Shu’ayb was very old. So he could not take the sheep to the water himself. Find one more reason in the chapter and say it with “because”.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “We have to be patient until the other shepherds go away.”
stopAndCheck.question: Why did the sisters come home early? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: Moses first understood what the sisters needed, and then he helped. Why is it important to listen before you help someone?

content.chapter: Chapter 8: A Simple Life in Midian
objectives: I can explain why Moses (pbuh) accepted the job in Midian.
I can put the main stages of his life in Midian in order.
I can separate background sentences from main events in a story.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Sort parts of the winter scene into background (It was winter, were crossing) and main events (took, saw, said), match words such as urgently and with patience with their meanings, then rewrite three sentences: After living as After he had lived, a because-reason as a so-result, and to get warm as so that we can get warm.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: STRAN-ger, UR-gent-ly, VAL-ley, HILL-side. Read the background slowly, then read “Suddenly, Moses saw a fire on the hillside.” a little faster.
content.lessonPlan: Look at The Fire hotspot. Why would a fire be important on a cold winter night? Listen once and follow the time words Later, After and Suddenly. Read the end of the chapter again and mark the background sentences and the main events.
discussionPoints: The family lived a simple life with patience for about ten years. What can a quiet, patient time prepare a person for?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “A New Family” and “The Fire”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Look for the time words: “Later, he married one of the sisters”, “After living in Midian for about ten years” and Suddenly. Write one event for each time word. Put the events in order again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about someone who spends a long time in one place, decides to leave and then changes plan because of a sudden situation. Use After living …, decided to, a past continuous background, Suddenly and to + verb for purpose.

whatToNotice: One kind act leads to an invitation, a job, a marriage and about ten years of simple life.
Notice the winter scene: “It was winter.” “It was getting dark and cold.” These sentences set the background before “Suddenly, Moses saw a fire on the hillside.”
readListen: Look at The Fire hotspot. Why would a fire be important on a cold winter night?
Listen once and follow the time words Later, After and Suddenly.
Read the end of the chapter again and mark the background sentences and the main events.
Open the picture hotspots “A New Family” and “The Fire” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find why Shu’ayb (pbuh) called Moses and what he offered him.
Middle: Find why Moses accepted the offer, who he married and how the family lived.
End: Find how long Moses stayed in Midian and what he saw on the way to Egypt.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: offered, stranger, valley, hillside.
“he was a stranger in Midian”: How does this explain why he needed a job and a house?
Write one sentence with offered and one with valley.
content.quickChallengeGuide: You will put five events in order, from Shu’ayb’s invitation to the fire on the hillside. Use the time words Later, After and Suddenly.
wrongAnswerSupport: Look for the time words: “Later, he married one of the sisters”, “After living in Midian for about ten years” and Suddenly.
Write one event for each time word.
Put the events in order again.
selfCheck: Can I give two reasons Moses accepted the offer?
Can I tell his life in Midian in four steps?
Can I tell a background sentence from a main event?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about someone who spends a long time in one place, decides to leave and then changes plan because of a sudden situation. Use After living …, decided to, a past continuous background, Suddenly and to + verb for purpose.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Explain in three sentences how Moses’s life changed in Midian.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “They lived a simple life with patience.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, how Moses lived in Midian for ten years.

thinkAloud.sentence: They were crossing a valley between mountains.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: I see a family walking in a dark valley in winter. There are mountains on both sides. It is cold, and suddenly a small fire appears on the hillside. Close your eyes and add one more detail from the text.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “he married one of the sisters.”
stopAndCheck.question: How long did Moses (pbuh) live in Midian? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: The family lived a simple life with patience for about ten years. What can a quiet, patient time prepare a person for?

content.chapter: Chapter 9: The Voice on the Mountain
objectives: I can describe the two signs Allah showed Moses (pbuh).
I can explain how Moses’s role changed after the message.
I can report an instruction with told + person + to.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Decide what “Upon this” means at the end of the chapter (right after this, and because of it), choose turned into, to go and became, then put the mountain scene in order with Then and Once more.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: SI-lence, GUID-ance, THUN-der-ing. Read each command clearly, with a short pause after it: “Put down your walking stick!”
content.lessonPlan: Look at The Call hotspot. Where was Moses, and what did he hear? Listen once and follow the commands and the actions. Read the end of the chapter again and mark what Allah told Moses to do in Egypt.
discussionPoints: After the message, Moses became a Messenger of Allah and headed to Egypt. How does a new responsibility change the way a person acts?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “The Call” and “Staff and Shining Hand”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the end of the chapter. Read the sentence that starts “These are signs of My power.” and the two sentences after it. Try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about someone who receives instructions, carries them out, takes on a new responsibility and begins a new task. Use an instruction, told + person + to, After this, became and a final sentence with the next action.

whatToNotice: The chapter follows a pattern: command, action, result. “Put down your walking stick!” leads to “Moses put down his staff on the ground.”
Notice “After this message from Allah, Moses became a Messenger of Allah, a prophet.” Became marks a new role.
readListen: Look at The Call hotspot. Where was Moses, and what did he hear?
Listen once and follow the commands and the actions.
Read the end of the chapter again and mark what Allah told Moses to do in Egypt.
Open the picture hotspots “The Call” and “Staff and Shining Hand” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find how the mountain was and what the voice said first.
Middle: Find what happened to the staff and to Moses’s hand.
End: Find what the signs were for, what Moses became and where he headed.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: silence, staff, signs, guidance.
“These are signs of My power.” What did the two signs show?
Write one sentence with silence and one with guidance.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The question asks why Allah showed Moses the staff and the shining hand. Read the end of the chapter and find what Allah says right after the shining hand.
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the end of the chapter.
Read the sentence that starts “These are signs of My power.” and the two sentences after it.
Try again.
selfCheck: Can I describe the two signs?
Can I explain how Moses’s role changed?
Can I report an instruction with told Moses to …?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about someone who receives instructions, carries them out, takes on a new responsibility and begins a new task. Use an instruction, told + person + to, After this, became and a final sentence with the next action.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Explain the two signs and the task in three sentences.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “Upon this, Moses (pbuh) headed to Egypt.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, what Moses saw and heard on the mountain.

thinkAloud.sentence: It was already dark and everywhere was very quiet.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: The writer describes the dark and the silence first. Then the thundering voice comes. The quiet makes the voice feel even stronger. Find one more word the writer chose with care and say what it adds.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “But it is not harmed.”
stopAndCheck.question: What happened to the walking stick? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: After the message, Moses became a Messenger of Allah and headed to Egypt. How does a new responsibility change the way a person acts?

objectives: I can explain what Moses (pbuh) tried first and why he then showed the miracles.
I can describe how the king and his advisors reacted.
I can use kept + -ing and had no choice but to.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Decide what “had no choice but to display the miracles” means (only one action was left), put five actions and results in order with Then and When, then rewrite effort, repetition and purpose: After he had made, again and again, and so that they could help.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: EF-fort, U-ni-verse, dis-PLAY, LOG-i-cal. The th in throne is soft, like in think. Read “The staff turned into a big snake!” with surprise.
content.lessonPlan: Look at the Harun hotspot. Why did Moses take a companion with him? Listen once and follow what Moses did first, second and third. Read the middle of the chapter again and underline “After making every effort to convince him”.
discussionPoints: The king and his advisors laughed at Moses instead of thinking about his words. Why is laughing at someone a weak answer to what they say?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “Harun” and “Signs in the Palace”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the middle of the chapter. Read the sentence with “After making every effort to convince him” and the sentence with “had no choice but to”. Put the steps in order, then try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a person who tries one solution, sees that it is not working and chooses another action. Use After making every effort, realized that, kept, had no choice but to, When and in order to.

whatToNotice: Moses tries words first; he shows the signs only when logical discussion does not work.
Notice “The Pharaoh kept refusing to believe in Allah.” Kept + -ing shows the refusal happened again and again.
readListen: Look at the Harun hotspot. Why did Moses take a companion with him?
Listen once and follow what Moses did first, second and third.
Read the middle of the chapter again and underline “After making every effort to convince him”.
Open the picture hotspots “Harun” and “Signs in the Palace” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find who went with Moses and how the king was sitting.
Middle: Find what Moses told the king, what the king thought and what Moses realized.
End: Find the two miracles, why Allah gave them to Moses and how the king reacted.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: effort, throne, universe, display.
“the Messenger from the Lord of the universe”: What does universe include?
Write one sentence with effort and one with display.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The statement is about when Moses showed the miracles. Read the middle of the chapter and find what Moses did before he threw down his staff.
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the middle of the chapter.
Read the sentence with “After making every effort to convince him” and the sentence with “had no choice but to”.
Put the steps in order, then try again.
selfCheck: Can I say what Moses tried before the miracles?
Can I explain why the Pharaoh did not change?
Can I use kept refusing and had no choice but to correctly?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a person who tries one solution, sees that it is not working and chooses another action. Use After making every effort, realized that, kept, had no choice but to, When and in order to.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Explain in two sentences why Moses showed the miracles.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “These were miracles of Allah.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, how Moses tried to convince the king.

thinkAloud.strategy: Ask a question while you read
thinkAloud.sentence: Moses (pbuh) had no choice but to display the miracles.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: I ask myself: Why did Moses have no choice? I look back. The Pharaoh kept refusing, and logical discussions did not work. Ask one more question and look for the answer in the chapter.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “his advisors and soldiers were standing around him.”
stopAndCheck.question: Who went to the palace with Moses (pbuh)? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: The king and his advisors laughed at Moses instead of thinking about his words. Why is laughing at someone a weak answer to what they say?

content.chapter: Chapter 11: The Miracle of the Staff
objectives: I can compare how the magicians and the king reacted to the same miracle.
I can explain the difference between looking like a snake and turning into one.
I can use still and because to explain a refusal that continued.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Decide if “they looked just like snakes” means the sticks really became snakes, fix three mistakes (who witnessed, let … live, Be rude), then complete the lines with still, because and to trouble.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: AR-ro-gant, WIT-nessed, ma-GI-cians. Bowed rhymes with loud. Read the magicians’ words strongly: “We believe in the Lord of Moses and Harun!”
content.lessonPlan: Look at The Magicians hotspot. What did they bring to the palace? Listen once and follow the reactions of Moses, the magicians and the king. Read the end of the chapter again and underline still and because.
discussionPoints: The magicians changed their minds when they saw the truth, but the king did not. What makes it hard for a proud person to change an opinion?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “The Magicians” and “The Huge Snake”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Find each name in the chapter: Moses (pbuh), the magicians, the king. Read the sentence around each name again. Match again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different situation in which an instruction leads to an action, one group changes its view and another person keeps resisting. Use Once or When, turned into, who, still, continued to and because.

whatToNotice: The same miracle leads to two opposite reactions: The magicians believe, but the king still refuses.
Notice “they looked just like snakes!” and “it turned into a huge snake”. Looked like describes how something seems; turned into is a real change.
readListen: Look at The Magicians hotspot. What did they bring to the palace?
Listen once and follow the reactions of Moses, the magicians and the king.
Read the end of the chapter again and underline still and because.
Open the picture hotspots “The Magicians” and “The Huge Snake” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find what the king said about the signs and who he invited.
Middle: Find how Moses (pbuh) felt, what Allah told him and what his staff did.
End: Find what the magicians did and said, and why the king still refused.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: made fun of, bowed down, arrogant, trouble.
“because he was arrogant”: How did arrogance stop the king from believing?
Write one sentence with made fun of and one with arrogant.
content.quickChallengeGuide: You will match three people or groups with their reactions. The middle of the chapter tells you how Moses felt; the end tells you what the magicians and the king did.
wrongAnswerSupport: Find each name in the chapter: Moses (pbuh), the magicians, the king.
Read the sentence around each name again.
Match again.
selfCheck: Can I compare the magicians’ reaction with the king’s?
Can I explain looked like and turned into?
Can I say why the king still refused, with because?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different situation in which an instruction leads to an action, one group changes its view and another person keeps resisting. Use Once or When, turned into, who, still, continued to and because.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Compare the magicians and the king in two sentences. Use “while”.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “The magicians who witnessed this miracle bowed down to Allah.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, why the magicians believed in Allah.

thinkAloud.sentence: Moses (pbuh) threw down his staff and it turned into a huge snake.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: I know this from Chapter 9. On the mountain, the staff turned into a snake for the first time. Now Allah uses the same sign in front of the magicians. Link one more sentence to an earlier chapter.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “they looked just like snakes!”
stopAndCheck.question: What did the magicians put on the ground? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: The magicians changed their minds when they saw the truth, but the king did not. What makes it hard for a proud person to change an opinion?

objectives: I can explain why the caravan moved slowly.
I can describe how Moses (pbuh) answered his people’s fear.
I can separate a plan (are going, will) from rules (must, should).
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Sort Moses’s words into the plan (We are going away, We will leave) and the rules (Get ready, must, should), rewrite a That’s why-result with so and managed to with succeeded in catching, then match words such as noticed, caravan and Calm down with their meanings.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: CAR-a-van, SE-cret, PAN-icked. Panicked has two syllables: PAN-ikt. Say “Calm down!” in a calm, low voice; the l in calm is silent.
content.lessonPlan: Look at The Night Journey hotspot. Why did they leave at night? Listen once and follow the journey from night to sunrise. Read the middle of the chapter again and find the sentence with That’s why.
discussionPoints: The caravan moved slowly because of the children and the old people, but nobody left them behind. What does this show about caring for the weakest people in a group?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “The Night Journey” and “The Army Behind Them”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the middle of the chapter. Read the sentence before “That’s why the caravan moved slowly”. Check when they left Egypt, then try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different group that must leave quietly, has members who cannot move fast, is followed by others and gets reassurance from its leader. Use an instruction, must or should, could not, That’s why, managed to and will.

whatToNotice: Moses gives a plan and rules; then come the slow caravan, the chase and the panic.
Notice “Calm down! Allah is with us and will show us the way to safety.” Moses answers panic with an instruction and a promise.
readListen: Look at The Night Journey hotspot. Why did they leave at night?
Listen once and follow the journey from night to sunrise.
Read the middle of the chapter again and find the sentence with That’s why.
Open the picture hotspots “The Night Journey” and “The Army Behind Them” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find what Allah told Moses and the rules Moses gave his people.
Middle: Find who was in the group and why the caravan moved slowly.
End: Find what the people saw at sunrise and what Moses said.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: secret, caravan, catch up with, panicked.
“But you must keep it secret.” Why was the secret important?
Write one sentence with caravan and one with panicked.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The question asks why the army could catch up with Moses and his people. Read the middle of the chapter and look for the words “That’s why”.
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the middle of the chapter.
Read the sentence before “That’s why the caravan moved slowly”.
Check when they left Egypt, then try again.
selfCheck: Can I explain why the caravan was slow?
Can I describe how Moses calmed his people?
Can I tell a plan from a rule in Moses’s words?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different group that must leave quietly, has members who cannot move fast, is followed by others and gets reassurance from its leader. Use an instruction, must or should, could not, That’s why, managed to and will.

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Explain in three sentences why the caravan was in danger.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “That’s why the caravan moved slowly.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, how Moses and his people left Egypt.

thinkAloud.sentence: Life became harder for them day by day.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: Who are “them”? The last chapter ended with the king saying to be rude to them, so “them” means Moses and his people. Find one more he, she or they and say who it is.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “We will leave at night.”
stopAndCheck.question: What did Moses tell his people to do? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: The caravan moved slowly because of the children and the old people, but nobody left them behind. What does this show about caring for the weakest people in a group?

objectives: I can tell the crossing of the sea in order.
I can explain why the Pharaoh’s last words were wrong.
I can turn the events of a story into a lesson with reminds us that.
content.pedagogy: Read and listen for meaning, find the evidence, do the Quick Challenge, then use the chapter’s Language Focus in your own sentences.
content.grammarFocus: Decide if when in “when we pray to Him, He always guides us” means one moment or every time, put the crossing in order from the command to the final consequence, then complete the lessons with to learn, that and to.
content.pronunciationFocus: Stress: PART-ed, en-SLAVE, VIS-i-ble. Drowned has one syllable: drownd. Read “The sea parted!” with surprise, and the lessons slowly and calmly.
content.lessonPlan: Look at The Path Through the Sea hotspot. What made the path possible? Listen once and follow the crossing step by step. Read the end of the chapter again and underline the lessons.
discussionPoints: The story reminds us that no one can enslave another human being. How does this lesson answer the Pharaoh’s cruelty in Chapter 1?
interactiveTips: Open the picture hotspots “The Path Through the Sea” and “The Final Lesson”.

differentiation.strugglingLearners: Go back to the beginning of the chapter. Read who gave the command to hit the sea and who made a path across the sea. Compare this with “The sea opened at my order”, then try again.
differentiation.fastFinishers: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different situation where a leader gives an instruction, an event changes the situation, a consequence follows and the group explains what it learned. Use an instruction, When, a result, to + verb for purpose and This reminds us that ….

whatToNotice: The chapter moves from events (the sea parts, the Pharaoh and his army drown) to lessons (no one can enslave another human being).
Notice “Look! The sea opened at my order.” The Pharaoh claims a miracle that Allah made.
readListen: Look at The Path Through the Sea hotspot. What made the path possible?
Listen once and follow the crossing step by step.
Read the end of the chapter again and underline the lessons.
Open the picture hotspots “The Path Through the Sea” and “The Final Lesson” and connect each one to a sentence in the chapter.
findAnswerInStory: Beginning: Find where the people were trapped and what Allah told Moses (pbuh) to do.
Middle: Find what happened to the sea and what the Pharaoh said to his soldiers.
End: Find what happened when the soldiers were midway, and three lessons of the story.
vocabularyInContext: Word Notes: trapped, parted, drowned, right path.
“They were trapped with the Red Sea in front and the king’s army behind them.” Why was there no way out?
Write one sentence with right path about a choice you make.
content.quickChallengeGuide: The question asks what the Pharaoh’s words show about him. Compare his words in the middle of the chapter with the beginning: Who told Moses to hit the sea, and who made the path?
wrongAnswerSupport: Go back to the beginning of the chapter.
Read who gave the command to hit the sea and who made a path across the sea.
Compare this with “The sea opened at my order”, then try again.
selfCheck: Can I tell the crossing in five steps?
Can I explain why the Pharaoh’s claim was false?
Can I state one lesson with reminds us that or shows that?
content.useWhatYouLearned: Language Focus, last activity: Write or say five connected sentences about a different situation where a leader gives an instruction, an event changes the situation, a consequence follows and the group explains what it learned. Use an instruction, When, a result, to + verb for purpose and This reminds us that ….

noteTaking.focus: Listen again with the book closed. Write one or two words in each box.
noteTaking.afterNotes: Use your notes: Write the three lessons of the story in three sentences.

mediationTasks.translation: Write “It again reminds us that no one can enslave another human being.” in your home language.
mediationTasks.homeRetell: Tell someone at home, in your home language, the lessons of the story of Moses (pbuh).

thinkAloud.sentence: It also shows that the only power over human beings is Allah.
thinkAloud.model: A good reader thinks: I want to sum up the whole book in one sentence. The cruel king said he was a god, but the sea closed over him. My sentence is: Only Allah has real power, and He guides those who pray to Him. Sum up the next paragraph in one sentence.

stopAndCheck.after: Stop after “Allah made a path for them across the sea!”
stopAndCheck.question: What did the Pharaoh say when he saw the road in the sea? If you cannot say it, read that part again.

content.reflectionPrompt: The story reminds us that no one can enslave another human being. How does this lesson answer the Pharaoh’s cruelty in Chapter 1?

metadata.title: Moses B1 — Self-Study Guide
metadata.subtitle: Read • Find • Check • Build • Use
metadata.estimatedStudyTime: About 25 minutes per chapter, plus the review pages at the end
metadata.whoIsThisFor: B1 learners who study the story of Prophet Moses (pbuh) on their own or at home.
learningGoals: Understand the 13 chapters of the story of Prophet Moses (pbuh).
Find evidence in the story before answering.
Use each chapter’s Language Focus in connected sentences.
Connect trust, responsibility and care for others with real actions.
recommendedUse: Study one chapter at a time.
Listen and read before the Quick Challenge.
Repair wrong answers with the text.
Do the Language Focus after you understand the chapter.
Do the review pages after Chapter 13.

readingDiary.intro: Keep this diary when you finish the book. Write short answers.
prompts: The date I finished the book:
My favorite chapter, and one reason:
One person in the story I want to remember, and why:
One sentence for a friend: “Read this book because …”
One new word I want to keep:
The next book I want to read in the library:

sections.title: 1. Make Your Plan
sections.text: This book has 13 chapters. Plan the whole book before Chapter 1: A clear plan helps you keep going and see your progress.
points: Choose your study days and how many chapters you will read each week.
If you like, choose a weekly goal in your Seyahatname. A new week starts on Monday.
Write one personal goal for this book, for example a skill you want to improve.
Save new words to My words and review them after one day, three days and one week. Short, spaced reviews help you remember.
Before Chapter 1, answer the “I can” statements in section 10, “Look Back”. Answer them again when you finish.

sections.title: 2. One Chapter per Session
sections.text: Each chapter takes about 25 minutes. Open “Study Path” for the steps of your chapter.
points: Preview the title and hotspots.
Listen and read for the main idea.
Find the evidence.
Do the Quick Challenge.
Do the Language Focus.

sections.title: 3. Listen and Read
sections.text: Use the audio twice: Once for the main idea, once to follow the exact words.
points: First listening: What is the chapter about?
Second listening: Follow the text line by line.
Replay one long sentence and say it with the same pauses.

sections.title: 4. Word Notes and Hotspots
sections.text: Each chapter has four Word Notes and two picture hotspots. Use them after you have tried to understand the sentence yourself.
points: Guess the meaning from the sentence.
Check the Word Note.
Write the word in a new sentence of your own.

sections.title: 5. Quick Challenge
sections.text: Answer before you read the feedback. If you are wrong, repair the answer with the text.
points: Find the part of the chapter the question is about: the beginning, the middle or the end.
Read the key sentence again.
Explain why the right answer is right, then try again.

sections.title: 6. Language Focus
sections.text: Each chapter has four Language Focus activities built from the chapter’s own sentences.
points: Activity 1 (Notice): Look at a sentence and its meaning.
Activities 2–3 (Build): choose, order, rewrite or correct forms.
Activity 4 (Use): Write or say five connected sentences about a different situation.

sections.title: 7. When It Is Hard
sections.text: Change how you study, not your goal.
points: Work on a few sentences at a time.
Use the hotspots to get the big picture first.
Write a one-line summary of the beginning, the middle and the end.
Focus on two Word Notes today.

sections.title: 8. Values in the Story
sections.text: The book contrasts the Pharaoh’s cruelty and pride with trust, responsibility and care for others. Connect each value to one action.
points: Trust in Allah: Act with trust even when you are afraid or sad (Chapters 2, 3).
Responsibility: Admit a mistake and ask for forgiveness (Chapter 5).
Helping others: Notice what someone needs, then act (Chapters 4, 7).
Humility: Pride kept the Pharaoh from the truth (Chapters 11, 13).
Human dignity: No one can enslave another human being (Chapters 1, 13).

sections.title: 9. At the End of the Book
sections.text: After Chapter 13, do the review pages in this order. Go back to the chapter when an answer is not clear.
points: Knowledge Check
Master Glossary
Places & People
Vocabulary Challenge
Language Review
Final Challenge

sections.title: 10. Look Back: My Level and My Learning
sections.text: Answer these statements before Chapter 1 and again after the Final Challenge: not yet, partly or yes. They come from the CEFR Companion Volume (Council of Europe, 2020) for level B1. One book is one step towards them, not a test.
points: Reading: “I can follow the plot of stories, simple novels and comics with a clear linear storyline and high frequency everyday language, given regular use of a dictionary.”
Speaking: “I can relate the plot of a book or film and describe my reactions.”
Writing: “I can produce straightforward connected text on topics that are familiar or of personal interest.”
Mediation: “I can convey information given in clear, well-structured informational texts on subjects that are familiar or of personal or current interest.”
Which study steps helped me most in this book, and why?
What was hard, and which strategy did I use?
What will I change in my plan for the next book?
